# Memdoor

> The workflow harness that makes a small model beat a frontier one, on your machine. Five Qwen3.8-27B agents beat Fable 5 on LiveCodeBench Hard, every run published. Ollama, llama.cpp, or any key. One binary, no account. Open source, on your gateway, on your key.

## Why Memdoor

- Token optimization: judged reads, tool selection and progress checks reduce unnecessary model input and stalled turns. Savings depend on the task; measurements are below.
- Single binary: deploy the CLI on macOS, Linux or Windows without Docker or Python. Connect over SSH to another machine with `memdoor --gateway ssh://you@box`.
- CLI, headless first: `memdoor run` takes a prompt, writes to stdout and returns a check-aware exit code for shell scripts, CI and cron. Resume the same conversation from a terminal, IDE or phone.
- Durable workflows, the deterministic harness: a graph of steps, each checked by its output, a gate where you want one, and a failed run resumed without repeating completed steps.

## What it is

Memdoor reads files, writes patches, runs the build and fixes what it broke, in the launch directory (`memdoor tui`). Doors onto the same gateway: `memdoor run "<prompt>"`, one headless turn (answer on stdout; exit code 0 checked / 2 unverified or a failing check / 3 it needed you); `memdoor workflow run <name> --wait`, a workflow from a shell or CI; `memdoor cron add`, a schedule; `memdoor acp`, the editor; `/remote` in a window or `memdoor remote <id>` from a script, the phone (link on stdout, conversation held on the relay); `memdoor resume <id>`, any of those runs in a window, live, same session. Guide: https://memdoor.ai/docs/headless; the gateway: https://memdoor.ai/docs/gateway

Every model call is on your key: OpenRouter, Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, DeepSeek, Baseten, Groq, xAI or a company AI gateway (`memdoor connect`, or export the key). Or no key: `memdoor connect local` finds janis on the box, or Ollama, llama.cpp, vLLM, LM Studio, and nothing leaves it (https://memdoor.ai/docs/open-weight). Memdoor adds nothing to the bill; code does not pass through memdoor.ai.

A decision model (Jev, by TypeSafe, hosted) in front of the chat model answers typed questions with a calibrated probability in under half a second. The judged excerpts go to it, through OpenRouter on your OpenRouter key or directly on a decision key (`memdoor connect typesafe`). On an Anthropic, OpenAI or Gemini key alone: off, no savings. Every host the binary can contact: https://memdoor.ai/docs/security. The harness acts on the answers:

- Judged reads: search hits, file sections and log lines are scored against the task; only what counts reaches the model.
- A toolbox sized to the turn: only the tools the request needs are sent (schemas were 37% of an edit turn's input when measured).
- A stop instead of a cap: a turn that stops making progress ends with what it has.
- `/model` pins any tool-capable model of a connected provider at its list price.

Measured over 44 paired runs (same tasks, decisions off and on, alternating): 22 of 22 passed each way; a question about the codebase went from 54,661 to 14,367 input tokens (−74%, three pairs); tasks that read the same files either way (an edit with a test, ten one-file fixes) changed nothing, within ±11%. Table: https://github.com/guregodevo/memdoor/blob/main/docs/features/DECIDE.md

## Workflows

Describe the steps; the coder writes the workflow, the deterministic harness: one YAML per task in `.memdoor/workflows/<name>/steps/`, run as a DAG by mario. Task kinds: `command` (a shell line; its exit code is the proof), `llm` (one model call), `agent` (a turn of the coder). Independent tasks run in parallel. A task is done when its target exists (a file, a command that exits 0); a target already true is skipped. An `external: true` task is a gate: the run waits until a person approves (`a` in /workflow, `memdoor workflow approve <run> <task>`). A failed run resumes at the failed step. `memdoor cron add --workflow <name>` runs one on your local cron. The catalog at /workflows lists workflows that exist as files and have run, each with a recording: team-solve, karpathy-recipe, ship, review, tui-check, issue-to-pr, release-check, digest.

## Results

- team-solve (2026-10-31): GVS5H's multi-agent harness (a planner, two ideators, a solver, a manager and a repair worker, each from a fresh context, talking only through files) rebuilt as a Memdoor workflow with the authors' exact prompts, temperatures, 128K reply cap and loop, on the same model, Qwen3.8-27B. On the first ten problems of the authors' LiveCodeBench Hard list, five passes each, graded on every hidden test: a mean of 9.8 of 10, against 9.6 for the authors' own harness and 8.0 for Fable 5 in a single call. Ten problems, not the authors' 100, so 9.8 and 9.6 are parity; on these ten the authors' own data put Fable 5 at 80 and their harness at 96, the gap the workflow reproduces (across their full 100: 92.4 and 90.4); contamination cannot be ruled out; Fable 5 was not given the harness. A run took a median of 40 minutes and $0.39. All 50 runs, every request, reply, program, grade and cost: https://github.com/guregodevo/memdoor/tree/main/examples/workflows/team-solve/bench/results/parity-5pass. The page: https://memdoor.ai/docs/team-solve. The Hacker News thread (front page, 2026-10-31): https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50320995
- decisions (2026-10): 44 paired runs, 22 of 22 passed each way; a question about the codebase went from 54,661 to 14,367 input tokens (−74%); edits unchanged within ±11%. https://github.com/guregodevo/memdoor/blob/main/docs/features/DECIDE.md

## Remote control (Pro)

`/remote` prints a link and a QR code. The page on the phone is the terminal, running on your computer. Screen and keystrokes are end-to-end encrypted; the relay on memdoor.ai forwards ciphertext. `/remote off` revokes the link.

## Price

- Free: the agent, the decision model (on an OpenRouter key or a decision key) and workflows with local schedules.
- Pro, $10/month: remote control through the memdoor.ai relay, and every workflow run's state kept on memdoor.ai, one table per workspace, so a workflow can wait on a task another workflow produced, from any machine; `memdoor workflow history` answers from anywhere. Coming: runs with the laptop closed. A seat never supplies a model key. https://memdoor.ai/pricing or `memdoor account subscribe`.
- Enterprise: the hosted state and the relay served for a company on its own instance or host, people and admins set up by us, invoiced. hello@memdoor.ai.

## Install

```
curl -fsSL https://memdoor.ai/install.sh | bash
export OPENROUTER_API_KEY=sk-or-...
cd your-project && memdoor tui
```

Windows: `irm https://memdoor.ai/install.ps1 | iex`
